isu_planting.title: Iowa State — Corn and Soybean Planting Date Considerations (2021)
isu_planting.basis: Iowa guidance: corn April 11–May 18; early soybean after April 11, finish by May 20. Suitable seedbed and soil temperature still govern planting.

nass_dates.title: USDA NASS — Usual Planting and Harvesting Dates (2010), p. 39
nass_dates.basis: Iowa usual harvest: grain corn September 21–November 21; soybean September 21–October 31. State-level historical ranges, not a forecast.

isu_water.title: Iowa State — Crop water use or evapotranspiration (2000)
isu_water.basis: Corn water demand peaks in July–August; tasseling through grain formation is sensitive. Soybean bloom and fruit set are sensitive. Calendar dates below are proxies, not observed stages.

isu_soy_water.title: Iowa State — Fight to the Finish for Moisture (2023)
isu_soy_water.basis: Soybean reproductive moisture demand extends into late July and August; exact proxy boundaries are demo assumptions.

marsden.title: Iowa State — Marsden Long-Term Rotation Study
marsden.basis: Published two-, three-, and four-year rotation examples in Boone County.

site_soils.title: Lazicki et al. (2016) — Marsden site description, section 2.1
site_soils.basis: Study coordinates 42°01′N, 93°47′W. Clarion and Nicollet loam and Webster silty clay loam occur at the site. These coordinates identify the study area, not a surveyed soil map unit.

clarion.title: USDA NRCS — Official Clarion Series Description (2005)
clarion.basis: Representative series profile, not a point-specific SSURGO extraction: surface loam; very deep and moderately well drained. Typical pedon horizons below.

location.name: Marsden Farm study area · Boone County, Iowa

soil.name: Clarion loam — representative upland profile
soil.note: Illustrative local series selection. Marsden also includes Nicollet and Webster soils. This is not a verified map-unit assignment at the representative coordinate. Soil texture supplies context only; no field access, erosion or water-stress model is applied.

assumptions: All dates and interval endpoints are inclusive. The same month/day rules repeat each year; weather does not shift this calendar.
Planned living cover is an assumed emergence-to-senescence interval, not measured canopy cover. No winter living cover is assigned to the corn–soybean plan.
Termination is a known empty rule for these annual cash crops. Missing crop calendars are unavailable, not zero risk.
No weather is downloaded by this feature. A supplied date/coverage range clips intervals; no values are extrapolated outside it.
